reader.requirement: At --std 85, for a sequential file whose FD has LINAGE and EXTERNAL, LINAGE-COUNTER must be one run-unit item shared by every program describing the external file; for an FD with LINAGE and GLOBAL, LINAGE-COUNTER (qualified or, where unique, unqualified) must be referenceable from every program directly or indirectly contained in the declaring program; a containee must not reach the LINAGE-COUNTER of a container's non-GLOBAL file.

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.Has(2014): below 2014 an unqualified LINAGE-COUNTER counts only the program's OWN LINAGE files when it has any (a container's GLOBAL LINAGE file is a candidate only for a program with none of its own); from 2014 every visible LINAGE file counts

reader.edition-search: read LinageFileOf whole; grep LINAGE_COUNTER()/LinageCounter over Compiler and Runtime; the GLOBAL inheritance (InheritedGlobals.AddContainerFiles) and the runtime counter (FileRegistry.LinageCounter, keyed by the connector name, so an EXTERNAL connector shares it) consult no edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: for a contained program with its own LINAGE file and a container's GLOBAL LINAGE file both visible, an unqualified LINAGE-COUNTER is the program's own at 85 (and 2002) but ambiguous from 2014; the global-name and external-item semantics of this rule are the same code at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers GLOBAL (direct containee, qualified and unqualified) and EXTERNAL (separately compiled program); not exercised: indirect containment, an FD with both GLOBAL and EXTERNAL, the 85 own-file arm of unqualified resolution, and the refusal of a non-GLOBAL container file's LINAGE-COUNTER. All probed here.

probes.expected: GF is GLOBAL and EXTERNAL: the indirectly contained D reads GF's counter 2 (OF and IN), its WRITE makes it 3 for the container; D's unqualified LINAGE-COUNTER is its own DF (6) at 85; the separately compiled X sees the external GF and BF counters (3, 3) and its WRITEs reach the main program (4, 4)

probes.printed: error COBOL5997: LINAGE-COUNTER referenced, but no file description entry contains a LINAGE clause; error COBOL0863: LINAGE-COUNTER OF 'NF': the qualifier shall name a file whose file description entry contains a LINAGE clause
probes.expected: NF is not GLOBAL, so its LINAGE-COUNTER is not a global name and the containee cannot reference it: refused

citations.check: OK  §1985:X.4.2.4 GR1  (4.2.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1

reader.notes: GLOBAL FDs reach containees through InheritedGlobals (non-GLOBAL ones are kept out), and the runtime counter belongs to the file connector, which an EXTERNAL FD shares across the run unit. The refusal of a non-GLOBAL container file is correct, but COBOL0863's text says the qualifier must name a file with a LINAGE clause when NF has one and is merely not visible: a wording imprecision, not a conformance failure of this rule.

refuter.evidence: lin3.cob (run lin3-001, --std 85): A has FD AF IS GLOBAL LINAGE 10 and contains B; B has FD BF IS GLOBAL LINAGE 20 and contains D; D has no FD. B's unqualified LINAGE-COUNTER compiles (own-file arm). D's 'DISPLAY "D UNQ=" LINAGE-COUNTER' is refused: 'lin3.cob(44,29): error COBOL5997: unqualified LINAGE-COUNTER with more than one LINAGE file: qualify by file-name'. At 1985 D specifies no file description entry with a LINAGE clause, so SRL2.8 requires no qualifier. Both LINAGE-COUNTERs are global names (GR1). X.1.3.8.2 GR1 puts in D's name set 'all global names which are defined in program A and in any programs which directly or indirectly contain program A', and GR3b.1 resolves to the nearest container's object ('The object in program A if the name is declared in program A'), which is B's BF counter. The program is legal and is rejected. Control lin4.cob (lin4-001): a container with one GLOBAL and one non-GLOBAL LINAGE file and a containee with none: 'D UNQ=02', right (only GF is visible). At --std 2023 (lin3-002) the same line is refused too, plus B's line under the 2014+ visible count. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:X.4.2.4 GR1 ... the text is in GR1'; 'OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SRL2.8 ... the text is in SRL2.8'; 'OK  §1985:X.1.3.8.2 ... it lies in GR1'; 'OK  §1985:X.1.3.8.2 ... it lies in GR3b.1'. Known note: kb/Work/PB5166 (landed) fixed only the arm where the program has a LINAGE file of its own; this zero-own, several-inherited arm is a sibling it did not reach. Under the other reading of SRL2.8 ('the source program' counts the whole nest), the reader's own lin1 D (own DF plus inherited GF, unqualified, accepted) would have to be refused. So the path fails the rule under either reading.
edition-sites-missed: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/CounterResolver.cs#LinageFileOf: the pre-2014 arm (!Edition.Has(2014)) narrows to the program's own LINAGE files only when it has some; with none, it falls back to the whole visible set instead of the nearest declaring program's GLOBAL LINAGE files (X.1.3.8.2 GR3b), unlike ReportOf, which uses Reports.NearestInScope
refuter.corrected: PARTIAL (rejects-legal-source, cause a: the 1985 arm of LinageFileOf is incomplete). At --std 85 an unqualified LINAGE-COUNTER in a contained program with no LINAGE file of its own, under containers at two or more levels that each declare a GLOBAL LINAGE file, must resolve to the nearest container's counter. It is refused with COBOL5997.

adjudication.reason: An unqualified LINAGE-COUNTER in a contained program is refused at 85 (COBOL5997, citing §2023), while the containing program's own unqualified reference is accepted. An unswept sibling of the landed kb/Work PB5166.
